title: A small, generic ‘preserve editorial intent’ prompt made outputs drift and failed promotion
description: A reusable editorial‑hierarchy instruction added to the Narrative user prompt did not preserve the supplied editorial intent; candidate runs consistently subordinated company identity and audience, made orchestration the central message, introduced unsupported claims, and the change was rejected and rolled back.
audience: Prompt engineers, Narrative/Compose maintainers, editorial leads responsible for model-driven outputs
rationale: This experiment is direct evidence that even short, generic prompt constraints can change the editorial hierarchy in systematic ways. For teams that control production prompts, the result argues for conservative change, controlled A/B testing, and hard promotion gates rather than assuming harmless reuse of editorial rules.
evidence:
• Candidate prompt added a single generic section “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis.” (Prompt diff in prompt-changes/Narrative.user.prompt.diff).
• Only Narrative.user.prompt.txt was changed; all other files, inputs, and model alias were identical.
• Candidate Narrative mean score 4.00/10 vs baseline 6.00/10; Compose mean 3.33/10 vs baseline 5.67/10 (tables in Run scores).
• All three candidate runs made orchestration central and introduced unsupported audience/validation framing (analysis section; failed gates C and D in every candidate run).
• Decision: “Do not promote.” Candidate not promoted; production prompt restored byte‑for‑byte (rollback SHA-256 match).
